resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and NYSFFLA give 1948. Forest Lookouts quotes a July 1959 article saying ranger Thomas Nugent had been stationed at the tower since 1947.
The register credits the NY State Conservation Commission (Bureau of Forest Fire Control) with the 1960 removal. NYSFFLA credits the Long Island State Park Commission.

resolved_conflicts.field: what happened to the service after 1959
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says the state abandoned lookout service and the title passed to Suffolk County. NYSFFLA's Long Island note says responsibility passed to town supervisors.

notes_for_editor: The 47-foot platform and the Oak Orchard location rest on NYSFFLA and the FFLA list; the platform was not seen. Access to the platform is inferred from NYSFFLA's note that visitors can see it; the wildlife area was not checked. The register's 'Town of North Port' location line is not used, and the register's 'concrete footings' detail is not used. An unread Facebook item in search results describes a 47-foot observation tower at Oak Orchard, with a different history; not cited. The 1945 Forest Lookouts item about a tower at Sunken Meadow State Park is not tied to this site, so it is not used. The 80-foot height is taken from the sources as written and converted to metres.
